title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Equipment Schedule Entry Gate
content:
## Proposal desk guidance

A tier of the Preventive Maintenance Agreements is proposed only for an equipment schedule that meets its entry gate. The gate has three tests, each read against the tier's entry figures on the proposal desk sheet (minimum units, maximum age, inspection requirement and inspection fee).

### Clause 1 — Minimum equipment count

The number of units on the equipment schedule the caller asks to cover must reach the tier's minimum equipment count, counted as the units standing on the site's equipment register at the day of the proposal, whatever their condition. The caller states which units are to be covered; the register decides which units stand at the site. A unit out of service still counts as standing on the register.

### Clause 2 — Maximum equipment age

No unit on the schedule may be older than the tier's maximum equipment age, counted in whole calendar months from the day the unit was installed to the day of the proposal, where a month completes on the day of the month matching the install day and, in a month that has no such day, on that month's last day; a unit whose age equals the maximum exactly still qualifies. The install date is taken from the unit's record on the equipment register.

Where a unit on the schedule exceeds the age limit of the requested tier, the schedule is either proposed at the highest tier whose age limit it meets or proposed with that unit excluded from coverage; the office never waives an age limit.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical dates).** A unit installed on 15 March of one year, measured against a 120-month limit, completes its 120th month on 15 March ten years later: a proposal dated that day finds the unit exactly at the limit and it qualifies; a proposal dated 16 March finds it older than the limit and it does not. A unit installed on 31 January completes each month on the last day of any month that has no 31st, so its 120th month completes on 31 January ten years on.

### Clause 3 — Pre-agreement inspection on file

A tier whose pre-agreement inspection requirement is set may be proposed only when an inspection work order for the same site is recorded as completed in the office records. The caller's statement that an inspection took place does not satisfy the clause; the completed work order in the office records does.

The pre-agreement inspection fee is charged when the inspection is performed and is credited against the first installment once the agreement activates.

### Truth table for the gate

| Unit count reaches the minimum | Every unit within the age limit | Completed inspection on file where the tier requires one | Tier may be proposed for the schedule |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes, or not required | yes |
| no | yes | yes, or not required | no |
| yes | no | yes, or not required | no, unless the schedule is re-proposed at a tier the unit's age meets or with that unit excluded |
| yes | yes | required and not on file | no |
